prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from persistent storage never get token_expiry_time recomputed in _initialize(), so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired access token as valid after a process restart. This skips the proactive refresh check at the top of async_auth_flow and forces a full interactive re-authorization on the first 401 instead of a silent token refresh. #1784 and #3251 both patch this by calling context.update_token_expiry(current_tokens) right after loading tokens in _initialize() - the same one-line root-cause fix in the same function. #2875 doesn't touch _initialize() at all; its own comment explicitly cites this exact root cause ('provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid') and instead patches the symptom by adding a reactive refresh-token attempt inside the 401 handler. (3 PRs)

prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id silently overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses. Both PRs add a check to reject a second in-flight request whose id is already in use. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id silently overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses. Both PRs add a check to reject a second in-flight request whose id is already in use. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(request_id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC int id `1` and string id "1" into the same key (can cause a spurious 409 between two actually-distinct ids) and does not guard against a numeric/string id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel. #3221 replaces the raw `str(id)` key with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that avoids both the int/str collision and the GET_STREAM_KEY collision, making it a more complete fix for the same routing-key collision bug (both reference the same underlying issue, #3060).

members.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
members.author: keurcien
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from persistent storage never get token_expiry_time recomputed in _initialize(), so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired access token as valid after a process restart. This skips the proactive refresh check at the top of async_auth_flow and forces a full interactive re-authorization on the first 401 instead of a silent token refresh. #1784 and #3251 both patch this by calling context.update_token_expiry(current_tokens) right after loading tokens in _initialize() - the same one-line root-cause fix in the same function. #2875 doesn't touch _initialize() at all; its own comment explicitly cites this exact root cause ('provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid') and instead patches the symptom by adding a reactive refresh-token attempt inside the 401 handler. clusters.pick_reason: #2478 fixes the pickling path at the MCPError base level: it introduces `_restore_mcp_error`, a dispatcher that already special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError (calling `.from_error()`) and falls back to `.from_error_data()` for every other subclass, so any MCPError subclass with a non-default constructor is covered, not just one. It also removes the `# pragma: no cover` on the `data` property, showing the payload-preservation path is now exercised by a test. #2555 only adds a `__reduce__` override local to UrlElicitationRequiredError; per its own docstring, the generic MCPError path still falls back to default `Exception.__reduce_ex__` for any other subclass, so it doesn't generalize. Since #2478's dispatcher already handles the UrlElicitationRequiredError case that #2555 targets, merging both would leave #2555's subclass-local `__reduce__` as a redundant override that shadows the base-class fix.

clusters.pick_reason: Explicitly closes the tracked issue (#2847) and is a rebase of an already-authored/reviewed prior PR (#2660), rather than an independent reimplementation. It introduces two clearly-documented locks with distinct, explained invariants (lock for short state mutations, refresh_lock for single-flight refresh with documented re-check-after-wait semantics), addressing the contention bug without changing the lock primitive. #3243 and #3252 modify the exact same lines (context.lock usage in async_auth_flow) with competing designs - #3243 replaces anyio.Lock with anyio.Semaphore across the board, #3252 keeps a single lock and only narrows its scope - and neither PR title/description ties back to the tracked issue, making them redundant alternate attempts at the same fix that would conflict with #2858 at merge time.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(request_id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC int id `1` and string id "1" into the same key (can cause a spurious 409 between two actually-distinct ids) and does not guard against a numeric/string id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel. #3221 replaces the raw `str(id)` key with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that avoids both the int/str collision and the GET_STREAM_KEY collision, making it a more complete fix for the same routing-key collision bug (both reference the same underlying issue, #3060).
